decisions.title: Keep interactive workflow controls model-only
decisions.rationale: Grade: Adopt. Reversibility: Tier 1 tool metadata rollback. Bottom line: declare research_mode and work_* workflow control tools model-only using the shared registration seam. Verified project fit: research transitions settle only at the top-level batch boundary; work_goal_complete/dirty_continue and verifier mutations terminate or change coded state and must not be nested in scripts. Upstream evidence: Pi 0.99+ extensions.md Tool exposure, types.d.ts ToolExposure and captured 0.87-to-1.0.2 diff explicitly provide model-only for orchestrating/interactive tools; nested calls have parentToolCallId and no transcript entries. Benefit: preserve direct visibility while excluding script-based control bypasses and ignored termination. Cost/risk: callers must use these tools directly; ordinary process_image, knowledge and research_note stay callable. Confidence: high. Recommendation: adopt now and assert exposures in the existing extension registration test. tooTechnical:false.
decisions.verification: PASS: node scripts/test-work-compaction-notifications.mjs; installed Pi metadata reports 1.0.2. Tool registration assertions cover model-only controls and ordinary nested-callable helpers.

decisions.title: Retain explicit role routing and image interpretation
decisions.rationale: Pi core Grade: Reject, Tier 2 routing/settings rollback: do not auto-enable codemode, replace explicit role routing with virtual/classifier models, tune sampling-by-thinking defaults, or remove the non-vision interpretation bridge. Project has deterministic leases, explicit user-selected role models and process_image for reasoning over references; native image generation/resizing does not replace interpretation. Upstream docs codemode/models/virtual-models and model registry type diff make these opt-in capabilities, not replacements. Benefit: retain control and avoid unmeasured cost/runtime changes; risks: benchmark required for future optimization; confidence high; recommendation retain incumbent routing, inherit opt-in host facilities.

decisions.title: Inherit host context, SDK, dynamic tools, model and TUI lifecycle changes
decisions.rationale: Pi core Grade: Not-our-problem, Tier 1 package rollback: hooks/context canonical semantics, SDK, native MCP dynamic loading, thinking/model catalog, samplingParamsByThinkingLevel, fullscreen/theme lifecycle, renderers, cache/model errors and OAuth are host-owned. Project uses supported context/boundary handlers, public modelRegistry and shared overlays; no removed node subpath or custom renderer override. Benefit inherit fixes without local shim; confidence high; recommendation no adapter.
decisions.costRisk: Ordinary upstream regression exposure; no duplicate provider, SDK, MCP or TUI implementation.

decisions.title: Migrate workflow launches and require the current RPC release
decisions.rationale: Candidate: migrate pi-subagents workflow launch contract. Grade: Adopt. Reversibility: Tier 1 local API/guidance rollback. Bottom line: replace RPC workflowScript with script and generated model instructions with workflow:true or script-path syntax. Project fit: spawnSubagentRpc (work-models.ts:11347) routes discoverer, leases, advisors and verifier launches; fixtures currently mock removed field and hide the break. Upstream evidence: pi-subagents 0.74.0 changelog, docs/extension-api.md:122, captured diff public-execution removal errors all reject legacy fields, even RPC. Benefit: restore coded specialist launches and prevent invalid advisor calls. Cost/risk: preserve stable keys, models, acceptance and async controls; update direct-mode work-role guard for the new public forms. Confidence: high. Recommendation: adopt now; focused checks compaction-notifications, settings and goal/launch fixture tests. tooTechnical:false; no explanation playbook needed.
decisions.additionalEvidence: Existing workflow compatibility candidate also raises pi-subagents peer floor to >=0.75.0 so installation cannot resolve a release that lacks current RPC or Pi 1.0 runner support.
decisions.reviewResolution: Recognize both slash and backslash workflow paths, including Windows .\guard-workflow.js, and fail closed for unreadable or oversized script paths.
decisions.verification: PASS: node scripts/test-work-compaction-notifications.mjs; node scripts/test-work-settings.mjs; node scripts/test-work-goal.mjs; node scripts/test-work-design.mjs. Installed metadata reports 0.75.0; current RPC fixtures assert script and absence of workflowScript.

decisions.title: Retain scoped child authority and coded work-item lifecycle
decisions.rationale: pi-subagents Grade: Reject, Tier 2 child-policy/settings rollback: no subagent_command grant, required-child extension registry, mission scheduler replacement or disabledFeatures optimization. Project uses explicit coded leases, scoped tool contracts and native acceptance; does not register required child policies, external runners or schedules, so requirements flag does not replace a current integration. Background checkpoint isolation remains mandatory. Benefit avoid speculative extra authority or duplicated mission lifecycle; confidence high; recommendation keep current per-launch restrictions.
decisions.costRisk: Extra child command authority or replacing native store-backed lifecycle would increase risk without demonstrated project benefit.

decisions.title: Inherit runtime, trust, model and resume-accounting improvements
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem, Tier 1 package rollback: inherit 0.71-0.75 async reload/reuse, terminal proof, cost/resume accounting, virtual model/preflight, model-only native orchestration tools, project trust/MCP and startup/runtime fixes from owner; ce telemetry already reconciles transcripts and launch IDs rather than copying plugin totals or deriving liveness from mtime. Recommendation no duplicate owner.
decisions.benefit: Managed launches inherit reliability fixes without a second runtime or accounting owner.

decisions.title: Recognize answered, skipped and cancelled decision batches
decisions.rationale: Grade: Adopt. Reversibility: Tier 1 result-normalization rollback. Bottom line: recognize 0.16.0 batch answers without treating a successful batch as unavailable, and honor an explicit Pause/Wait selection in an answered batch. Project fit: recordWorkGoalAskUserResult currently requires details.response and incorrectly sets unavailable for every batch; askUserPauseSelection reads only the single result. Coded dirty/improvement approvals remain intentionally single-question and reject batches. Upstream evidence: README Result details, public schema and index.ts executeBatch define aligned questions/answers with answered or skipped status and empty answers on cancellation; malformed/UI failures throw. Benefit: independent decision batches work safely with work-goal continuation; skipped questions remain unresolved. Cost/risk: validate full alignment and require every question answered before clearing fallback-unavailable. Confidence: high. Recommendation: adopt now with single/batch/cancelled/skipped/pause regression cases. tooTechnical:false.
decisions.verification: PASS: node scripts/test-work-goal.mjs; node scripts/test-work-compaction-notifications.mjs. Regression cases cover single, complete batch, skipped, cancelled, malformed alignment and Pause/Wait.

decisions.title: Retarget the optional remote-answer patch to the abortable UI lifecycle
decisions.rationale: Grade: Adopt. Reversibility: Tier 1 patch-helper rollback. Bottom line: retarget the opt-in patch to current public UI lifecycle using an abortable race; do not mutate the installed package during catch-up. Project fit: packaged scripts/patch-ask-user-remote-answer.mjs and test-work-ask-remote.mjs promise remote answers but installed 0.16 is unpatched, env flag unset; test assumes a patch even when disabled. External evidence: captured ask-user diff and current execute(), dialog options and runCustomPrompt signal cleanup. Benefit: preserve optional single-question remote answering without leaking losing UI and make default verification independent of installed patch state. Cost/risk: batch remote answering remains unsupported and local UI remains available; patch must still fail loudly on anchor drift. Confidence: high. Recommendation: adopt with temp-source patch/idempotence and abort-race checks. tooTechnical:false.
decisions.verification: PASS: node scripts/test-work-ask-remote.mjs. Patches installed 0.16 source in memory only, asserts idempotence, syntax, anchor-drift rejection, winning-side races, abort cleanup and listener disposal. Live opt-in TUI/intercom interaction not exercised; installed source remains untouched.

decisions.title: Pin forwarded answers to the exact local recipient and session
decisions.rationale: Grade: Adopt. Reversibility: Tier 1 bridge guard rollback. Bottom line: keep remote ask answers pinned to the exact local peer that received that prompt, refuse crossMachine (ssh-asserted) or trustedLocal:false messages, and reset bridge state on shutdown. Project fit: work-ask-remote.ts currently learns peerId from every intercom message then accepts any matching ANSWER token; 0.16 adds cross-machine relay messages to that same message type. Upstream evidence: README cross-machine section, types.ts CrossMachineProvenance and Message.crossMachine, index.ts message renderer persist details.message; identities are explicitly unverified. Benefit: a new peer or SSH-asserted origin cannot hijack a forwarded human decision. Cost/risk: optional bridge continues local-only; actors use local UI for remote-origin decisions. Confidence: high. Recommendation: adopt with cross-machine, wrong-peer, correct-peer and shutdown tests. tooTechnical:false.
decisions.reviewResolution: The original POV is preserved above. Independent review and upstream broker/broker.ts:481 establish that trustedLocal:false also describes ordinary Windows local peers, not remote provenance. The implementation therefore rejects crossMachine at either nesting, not trustedLocal:false; it retains exact recipient pinning and shutdown reset. Windows local answering has a regression check.
decisions.verification: PASS: node scripts/test-work-ask-remote.mjs; wrong peer, both crossMachine locations, Windows local trustedLocal:false, correct recipient, forward-before-answer and shutdown cases. Live broker/TUI interaction not exercised.

decisions.title: Keep transport, peer lifecycle and handover package-owned
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Tier 1 package rollback. Keep handover, Herdr location/CLI, session identity claim, broker heartbeat and scope/steering lifecycle package-owned; ce-workflow already uses exact IDs and supported outbox, not broker or pane ownership. Benefit: inherit upstream improvements without duplicate transport. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no new peer orchestration or automatic handover.
decisions.costRisk: Ordinary upstream regression exposure; do not automatically transfer workflow authority between sessions.

decisions.title: Inherit pi-goal recovery, stale-context, settings, and documentation fixes
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: keep pi-goal 0.54.8 package-owned and make no ce-workflow compatibility adapter. Verified project fit: ce-workflow's coexistence path only reads the canonical custom goal-state entry and sends public /goal pause and /goal resume commands; the installed persistence source still serializes data.goal under customType goal-state, and the public commands remain unchanged. Verified upstream evidence: the installed 0.54.8 README, managing-goals and settings references, package metadata, source, and captured 0.54.4-to-0.54.8 artifact show internal transient-stream classification, stale extension-context cancellation, menu/settings lifecycle, and documentation/build changes while preserving the coexistence surface. Benefit: pi-goal users receive safer recovery and lifecycle behavior without duplicate state ownership. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local adapter.

decisions.title: Inherit configuration, diagnostics and bounded analysis without a local shim
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Tier 1 package rollback. Keep global agent-dir config discovery, diagnostic save/freshness/dispositions, scanner retirement, Windows paths and bounded spawning package-owned. Verified project fit: ce-workflow consumes lens_diagnostics source=lsp and module_report, not config paths or analyzer internals; immutable verifier contracts remain checkpoint-bound. Upstream: complete 4.3 changelog, docs/agent-tools.md and captured tool/config diffs; public parameter contract unchanged, explicit too-large outcome now documents 5000-line/2MiB limits. Benefit: better diagnostics with no local adapter. Cost/risk: work-models.ts exceeds LSP bound; do not misreport it clean. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local shim or verifier capability expansion.
